title: Multi-Key Known-Key Notions for Iterated Even–Mansour
summary: Single-key known-key indifferentiability is too restrictive; defining and analyzing multi-key indifferentiability and correlation intractability for IEM and ideal-cipher constructions remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the iterated Even--Mansour (IEM) cipher and ideal-cipher constructions, study multi-key known-key indifferentiability by extending the known-key setting to $m_0$ independently random challenge keys $k_1,\ldots,k_{m_0}$ supplied as input to the construction or distinguisher, and determine the corresponding security notion. Also formulate and analyze the matching challenge-key correlation-intractability notion, requiring that a relation or machine $M$ produce outputs $(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ involving only the challenge keys $k_1,\ldots,k_{m_0}$. The unresolved task is to establish these multi-key notions and their consequences for the IEM and ideal-cipher constructions, since the single-key known-key formulation is too restrictive and the study of these proposed notions remains open.

scope.domain: Multi-key known-key security notions for iterated Even–Mansour and ideal-cipher block-cipher constructions.
assumptions: The challenge keys are independently random.
parameters: m_0: number of challenge keys supplied as input to the construction or distinguisher
k_1 through k_{m_0}: independently random challenge keys
M: relation or machine producing the challenge-key-constrained outputs
m: number of output components produced by M
scope.unresolved_remainder: Define and analyze multi-key known-key indifferentiability and matching challenge-key correlation intractability, and determine their consequences for IEM and ideal-cipher constructions.

citations.label: On the Provable Security of the Iterated Even-Mansour Cipher Against Related-Key and Chosen-Key Attacks

progress.summary: The source identifies the single-key known-key formulation as too restrictive and sketches multi-key indifferentiability and correlation-intractability variants. It explicitly leaves the study of these notions to future work.
citation_labels: Benoît Cogliati et al., On the Provable Security of the Iterated Even-Mansour Cipher Against Related-Key and Chosen-Key Attacks
